key_insight: Realistic Lindbladian noise imposes approximate symmetry constraints on Pauli fidelities, letting one infer a usable gauge from the error type even when the error magnitude is unknown.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum hardware teams a practical way to reduce ambiguity in gate-noise characterization and improve SPAM-error identification and mitigation.
method: Use Lindbladian perturbation theory on Clifford gates such as CZ, CNOT, iSWAP, SWAP, and ZZπ/2.
Compare Pauli fidelities of P and U_g P U_g† to derive symmetry relations and selection rules.
Identify which error classes break symmetry at first order versus only at second order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both numerical validation and experimental confirmation on IBM Kingston.
watch_item: The symmetry-based gauge fixing is approximate and depends on correctly knowing the noise class; unmodeled or strong nonperturbative errors may weaken the selection rules.
paper_title: Symmetries of Pauli Noise from Lindbladian Dynamics
